body.statement: The universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) may be chosen so that every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) obeys \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2>0\) and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P_U\left(\left|\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le\frac{C_0B\lambda_n}{c^2n\varepsilon^2}.\] Consequently the class supremum is at most \(C_0Bd/(c^2n\varepsilon^2)\), so the ratio converges to one uniformly whenever \(d_n=o(n)\), including the sharp normal regime.
body.justification: This expanded-regime ratio statement is a candidate downstream consequence and is not treated as established before D0 verification.
body.gap: Propositions 5.3--5.4 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, while \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} explains why exact variance cannot replace this bound.
body.consumer: If proved, it would make the candidate normal frontier usable with observed outcomes rather than the inaccessible exact variance.
